properties.otherAdvice:
Vehicles between 15 and 28 tonnes are now able to access the valley with Council permission, under stop/slow conditions.

As the area remains a construction site, safety procedures must be followed.

For vehicles between 15 and 28 tonnes to access the site:

  • Please email the Manager Transport and Public Access, Nicole Hume at nhume@bmcc.nsw.gov.au with at least two working days’ notice to obtain a permit for the heavy vehicle access.
  • A permit will be required to be carried and shown to traffic control on site. Traffic controllers will then coordinate access through the site.

Please note that if the same vehicle needs to access the valley multiple times, only one permit will be required. Vehicles over 15 tonnes that are not scheduled to enter the valley will be turned back to ensure safety is maintained on site.

High volumes of holiday traffic are expected approaching Sydney Airport during peak holiday periods.

Sydney Airport advises travellers to arrive two hours before domestic flights and three hours before international flights, to check-in online and pre-book parking.

For details about known holiday traffic pinch points, see the NSW Holiday and Journey planning website and the pinch point journey planning tool.

High volumes of holiday traffic are expected approaching and through Blackheath, Mount Victoria and Lithgow during peak holiday travel periods.

When queueing begins eastbound at Mount Victoria, a Traffic Management Plan is put in place to prevent breakdowns on Victoria Pass. Stop/slow traffic conditions will be put in place for eastbound traffic, with traffic controllers on site to direct motorists.

For details about known holiday traffic pinch points, see the NSW Holiday and Journey planning website and the pinch point journey planning tool.

• Light vehicles can use Olympic Hwy and Silo Rd.

Work on the Coffs Harbour bypass will pause from Friday 20 December 2024 to Monday 6 January 2025 inclusive to reduce impact during the busy holiday period. However, the current reduced speed limit of 60km/h for the project will remain in place throughout the shutdown period.

For details about known holiday traffic pinch points, see the NSW Holiday and Journey planning website and the pinch point journey planning tool.

High volumes of holiday traffic are expected approaching Heatherbrae, Hexham and towards Beresfield during peak holiday travel periods.

There are multiple projects underway at this location, including the Pacific Hwy improvements at Hexham and the M1 extension to Raymond Terrace, which can impact travel times. A reduced speed of 60 km/h will be implemented along the length of the project and will remain in place throughout the holiday period.

For details about known holiday traffic pinch points, see the NSW Holiday and Journey planning website and the pinch point journey planning tool.

High volumes of holiday traffic are expected approaching the NSW-Queensland border during peak holiday travel periods.

M1 Pacific Mwy upgrades in Queensland could cause significant traffic delays north of the NSW border. While this work will pause during the Christmas and new year period, heavy congestion is expected on the Pacific Motorway north of the NSW border at most times. You can toggle to view traffic information supplied by QLD on Live Traffic NSW.

For details about known holiday traffic pinch points, see the NSW Holiday and Journey planning website and the pinch point journey planning tool.
